fields.title: Tighten the workspace lint table with suppression reasons, unwrap, leftover-macro, assertion-message and missing-docs lints
fields.description: Packages inheriting [workspace.lints] enable only cognitive_complexity, too_many_lines and fn_params_excessive_bools, while native Runledger denies unwrap_used, dbg_macro, todo and reasonless suppressions and native Runlimit warns on missing_docs. Add clippy::allow_attributes, clippy::allow_attributes_without_reason, clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::dbg_macro, clippy::todo, clippy::missing_assert_message and rust missing_docs at warning level, enforced by the existing -D warnings verification. Replace #[allow] with reasoned #[expect] where the lint fires in every compiled configuration; keep any configuration-dependent suppression explicit with a reason. Remove the now-redundant crate-local #![warn(missing_docs)] attributes.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Workspace lint inheritors pass all four Clippy configurations with the new lints; every remaining suppression states a reason; docs/testing.md lint contract and the docs/status.md row describe the table; bash scripts/verify.sh passes on 1.98.1 and the outcome is recorded here.

fields.title: Own work-to-finalization sequencing and cleanup acquisition handoff

data.text: Plan and assessment: T1 reuse command run_work as a generic private phase poller, add inert PhasedOperation with work-only callback and delayed FinalizationScope callback, retained typed phase reports and owner/observer completion. Parent cancellation affects both phases; owner loss cancels work only and retained coordinator attempts finalization. T2 opaque Acquired handle/finalizer returned by native factory, consumed by CleanupSlot::acquire before exposing handle, preserving LIFO. T3 migrate outbound facade example and add compile-fail/runtime boundary controls; document raw OperationPhases and manual slot registration as weaker compatibility paths. T4 full pinned verify.sh once after focused checks and additive API surface review. Dependencies T1/T2 -> T3 -> T4. No destructive cut intended. Risks: work destruction panic, finalizer factory panic, ready output retention, parent-vs-owner cancellation, unpolled/drop, resource pairing before native factory completion. Runtime death/non-yielding tasks, unsupervised descendants and remote effects remain outside local proof.

Implementation progress: 12 phased-operation failure cases, 4 acquisition cases and 4 Send-contract checks passed; 78 core doctests passed. Canonical wait now returns PhasedFailure::Report whenever either phase fails (independent typed outcomes retained), preventing ? from treating completion as success. Raw outbound example kept explicit because generic cancellation-first polling must not discard its transport-specific ready Exchange; recorded in ADR-010.

fields.title: Assess phase success proofs and protected acquisition boundaries

data.text:
Root-cause assessment of PR #84 following branch panel; related implementation batter-jxj2 and follow-up batter-17fe. This is a new source assessment, not another reviewer vote or repair-loop pass. No reviewed source/index changes.

Panel findings classify as: unreachable example branch = local migration mistake plus erased checked-success fact; stale cleanup guidance = incomplete migration plus canonical/escape-hatch paths sharing capability; zero-reserve coverage = missing execution evidence, not demonstrated faulty arithmetic.

Deeper API evidence:
1. operation/phased/report.rs:137-145 returns SharedPhasedReport for checked success; the same general report is accepted by public PhasedFailure::Report at 110-112. Compile probe confirms arbitrary general report can be reclassified as failure. PhaseOutcome::result() exposes returned Ok independently of late interruption/destruction, so agents can accidentally confuse a returned value with accepted success. Existing runner correctly checks all evidence before Ok; no driver defect claimed. Recommended bounded design: opaque checked success and checked failed-report views constructed only by library classification, success access to values without re-check/unwrap, canonical phase classification accounting for all evidence with raw returned evidence explicitly available on failed outcomes. Preserve independent work/finalization failure and late returned values. Existing CommandSuccess provides local precedent; keep shared observation and existing owner cancellation.

2. cleanup/acquisition.rs:79-89 protects Ready(Acquired) to registration, not native Ready(resource) to Acquired. Arbitrary caller async factory owns resource and can await/panic before returning pair. Executed external read-only probes compiled against built batter-core: after simulated successful acquisition then pending await, cancelling leaves acquired=true, registered_finalizers=0; nested native future returning Ready then panicking on destruction likewise leaves registered_finalizers=0. Existing test PanicOnDrop<Acquired> verifies only outer future destruction, not nested native acquisition. Explicit documented partial-factory responsibility means this is a limitation/design gap relative to broader agent-native acquisition goal, not a contradiction of the narrow documented factory-return guarantee. No real resource leak/remote failure demonstrated.
Recommended fix shape: canonical supported-resource entry points own native acquisition and predetermined cleanup policy, consuming reservation/spec; register before destroying ready native future, before user projection/post-acquisition callbacks, before exposing handle. Supply opaque/sealed supported adapter capabilities so arbitrary app async glue is not treated as equivalently protected. Keep generic pair-producing acquisition/manual registration as explicit lower-level contract. Rust cannot inspect arbitrary future internals or prove remote effect/correct cleanup association. Existing batter_sqlx::pool_in at lib.rs:561 owns construction/register/return and is a relevant adapter precedent; don't move adapter ownership into core or broaden claim to all native futures.

3. Zero reserve is explicit policy: both deadlines same, no finalization opportunity after work timeout. Clock passage needs runtime checks, not a promise encoded by typestate. Keep single absolute deadline arithmetic; add paused-time existing-pair execution test proving both deadline failures/no finalizer factory invocation. No new generic runtime needed.

Fix validation shape: compile-fail success/failure proof forging and canonical manual-handoff misuse; runtime native Ready(resource) destructor panic, cancellation before native Ready, registration before any supported handle exposure/post-acquisition async work, both phase evidence preservation/late interruptions, owner/waiter policies, zero-reserve expiration. Existing full verification evidence remains; no code changed, so no matrix rerun.

Artifacts: /tmp/batter-phase-assessment/probe.rs and probe-output.txt. Probes are synthetic local boundary evidence; no upstream/remote effects claimed. Public signature changes need documented migration and shim decision per repository policy; do not silently implement redesign during assessment.
